summary: Frontend-only regression testing completed for the parent portal login crash. Parent demo login, repeated persona switching, full parent tab navigation, and delayed workspace-load checks passed without the reported runtime exception.

integration_issues.issue: Console logs show two 401 responses from /api/auth/me before session is established. Flow still proceeds normally via demo login.

action_items: Optionally suppress or handle expected pre-session /api/auth/me 401 noise to keep console cleaner during startup.
Keep defensive workspace defaults in place; consider normalizing /workspace/{role} responses to EMPTY_WORKSPACE shape if backend ever returns null/partial payloads.
critical_code_review_comments: PortalLayout now initializes workspace with EMPTY_WORKSPACE and renders a loading gate before Outlet content, which prevents child-page dereference crashes during workspace fetch latency.

refresh() currently applies setData(res.data) directly; if API returns null/partial shape in future, child pages using data.children[0] may regress. Consider fallback merge with EMPTY_WORKSPACE in state assignment.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for requested parent-login crash regression coverage

context_for_next_testing_agent: Executed three auth-switch cycles (parent -> logout -> staff -> logout -> parent), navigated Parent Today/My child/Home practice/Schedule/Home activities/Classroom updates/More, and validated delayed /api/workspace/parent behavior with explicit loading-state visibility. Exact reported error string was not observed in DOM, console, or page errors.
rca of the issue: Original crash pattern is consistent with a null workspace dereference race: Parent.jsx reads data.children[0] and similar fields that fail when workspace is null during initial render. The fix in PortalLayout (EMPTY_WORKSPACE initialization + loading guard) prevents rendering dependent views with null workspace while fetch is in progress. Repro validation with 8s artificial delay showed workspace-loading visible and no runtime crash.
